nodes.label: measure rigidity (MR)
nodes.plain: Every measure on the dual of the unit-vector ring that the unit-vector group preserves, and that gives no mass to the archimedean part, is a multiple of Haar measure. The hinge of every result above four at a field, and of the collapse.
nodes.quote: every U_F-invariant finite positive measure on R̂ with τ(E) = 0 is a multiple of Haar measure (MR(F))
nodes.grade: PE-2 two derivations blind to each other (X02D, X02V)

nodes.label: the collapse

routes.name: The classical interval, in the kernel
routes.about: Both ends of 5 ≤ χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7, checked by Lean's kernel on the standard three axioms (row 33). Not new mathematics: the ground every route stands on.

routes.name: Five, algebraically, through measure rigidity
routes.about: χ(ℚ(√47)²) = 5 gives χ(ℝ²) ≥ 5 with no witness object (rows 120–121). A second proof of a held bound — it moves no value, and its publication waits on MR in Lean.

routes.name: The regularity wall, toward seven
routes.about: Given MR the plane's number is its measurable number (rows 128, 130); that is seven iff vanishing holes cannot save a colour (row 131). R's reduction splits it into door (A), no tight six-map, and door (B), the cone scale (FS-111). Door (A) is closed under Condition 5 (row 134); with unit arcs FS-112 reduced it to one statement, the global step (FS-114). Card 1 (FS-111, two minds) found the two doors are two routes, not halves: FS-114's NO reaches seven only through the map step (FS-121), or route R's forced pair (FS-122) with the NO idle — and each third statement is the answer restated; route M's rungs hold down to the pinch at a junction (FS-120).

routes.name: The YES side: a tight six-map
routes.about: A tight six-map at bounded complexity gives vanishing holes (W-EQ-K), hence χ(ℝ²) ≤ 6 with no MR. The held positives (the strip, the disk) are tight fragments that stop at a pinned corner.

routes.name: The YES side at unbounded complexity
